predecessors.name: Stem Duchy of Saxony
predecessors.text: the diocese's lands round Münster, 'Created on collapse of Saxony: 1180'

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: Prussia 'took the larger eastern share', possession taken in March 1803 (infobox 'Secularised to Prussia: 1802')

successors.name: Duchy of Oldenburg (Grand Duchy from 1815)
successors.text: 'Oldenburg gained the northern part (Vechta and Cloppenburg)'

successors.name: Duchy of Arenberg
successors.text: Arenberg, Looz-Corswarem, Salm and Croÿ 'received other parts as compensation'

ledger.x: 1180: the Prince-Bishopric of Münster appears on the collapse of Saxony ('Created on collapse of Saxony: 1180'); the bishop had the city's administration from 1173 and imperial princely rank from 1220.
1252: the see buys Vechta and Meppen.

1803: Oldenburg receives the north: 'The Duchy of Oldenburg received much of the Prince-Bishopric of Münster' (mediatisation page); the Münster page: 'Oldenburg gained the northern part (Vechta and Cloppenburg)'.
1803: Arenberg, Looz-Corswarem, Salm and Croÿ 'received other parts as compensation'.
March 1803: Prussia takes possession of its eastern share under the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss.
1803: Prussia receives the eastern share: 'Prussia took the larger eastern share, which it took possession of in March 1803'; 'In 1815 Prussia was given the southern part (Oberstift).'

wars.name: Münster Rebellion
wars.outcome: The prince-bishop's army takes the Anabaptist city on 24 June 1535; the leaders are executed in January 1536.

wars.name: Münster-Dutch war and the Treaty of Cleves
wars.outcome: Galen was 'compelled ... to make a disadvantageous peace in 1666 in Cleve'; no border moved on the pages opened.

wars.name: Franco-Dutch War (Münster's part)
wars.outcome: Galen allied with Louis XIV and took Groenlo, Deventer and Coevorden; 'In October 1674 he withdrew his troops from the Dutch Republic', and in 1675 turned against France.

wars.name: Galen's war with Sweden over Bremen-Verden
wars.outcome: Galen 'attacked Charles XI of Sweden, and conquered the Duchy of Bremen'; the page gives no dates and no lasting gain.

certainty.note: The pages give towns and districts, not boundaries; the Oberstift and the Niederstift (Vechta, Meppen, Cloppenburg) were joined only by a strip.
